text: Thank you for that detail; a dry cough persisting for two months is considered chronic. To understand if this is related to an environmental trigger, do you smoke, or do you notice the cough worsens when you are exposed to dust, cold air, or pets?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't smoke. The cough actually seems to get worse when I'm exposed to dust or cold air, but it hasn't changed much around pets. I also notice some heartburn lately, which makes me wonder if my allergies or stomach are related.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the worsening with cold air and dust, along with recent heartburn, I want to rule out gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) which can mimic asthma. REQUEST TEST: Upper GI endoscopy. Also, have you noticed if taking antacids or eating smaller meals makes the cough or heartburn better?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your upper GI endoscopy came back normal, we can likely rule out severe esophageal issues. To narrow this down further, does your cough improve significantly after taking an antacid or eating smaller meals, and have you been taking any new medications recently?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the endoscopy was normal and antacids aren't helping, let's explore if this could be post-nasal drip or sinusitis instead. Do you experience frequent throat clearing, a sensation of mucus dripping down your throat, or any nasal congestion or sinus pressure?

Additionally, to rule out early signs of lung pathology, I need to check your oxygen saturation and listen to your lungs. Please hold still while I perform a quick physical exam of your respiratory system.
